answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. If several new accounts appear on an island of activity, their deposits remain independently at risk: when linked accounts coordinate a provable double-spend or false report, the protocol confiscates stake and pays a portion to the reporter. The vine of cheap account creation no longer yields cheap influence; an attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and lose it when caught, while a plume of honest agents can keep operating.
